CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain following trampoline park injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who injured his right knee at a trampoline park with his wife one week ago. He heard a snap and experienced instant pain when landing on the trampoline. This was his first visit to a trampoline park, and the activity was purely recreational rather than part of an exercise routine. He reports that the pain is located on the lateral (outside) aspect of the knee. He took Tylenol for pain management, which provided minimal relief. He has attempted conservative management with elevation only, and no ice or heat was applied. He reports a slight limp and can bear weight, though with difficulty. He denies regular exercise and reports his exercise regimen is inconsistent. He states he does not like coming to the doctor.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No fever, chills, or dyspnea reported. Patient reports blood sugars "a little bit better" recently. Reports elevated blood pressure readings. No other systemic complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily (takes most days as remembered)
2. Metformin 500 mg daily
3. Tylenol as needed for pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient does not exercise regularly and reports inconsistent exercise habits. Recently participated in recreational trampoline park activity. Denies specific dietary plan. Attempts to watch carbohydrate intake but does not count or track. Denies keto diet. Prefers not to seek medical care.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure elevated at approximately 180/80.
General: Alert and oriented.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm appreciated, no murmur appreciated.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally.
Right Knee: Tenderness to palpation on lateral aspect; no tenderness on medial aspect. Able to bend and straighten knee. Gait reveals slight limp. Able to bear weight with some difficulty. Ecchymosis and edema noted along the lateral aspect of the knee. No effusion appreciated. Decent range of motion maintained but with associated pain on some movements.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain, lateral ligament strain: Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. Referred to physical therapy for strengthening of surrounding muscles and injury prevention. Reassured that this is a common injury that typically heals on its own. Further imaging can be considered if pain persists.

2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Ordered echocardiogram to evaluate for any cardiac concerns. Patient's blood pressure remains elevated and may require medication modification. Discussed need for blood pressure monitoring at home, though patient has not yet obtained a home blood pressure cuff.

3. Diabetes mellitus: Ordered A1C to assess long-term glucose control. Patient reports checking blood sugars 4-5 times per week as remembered. Advised to increase monitoring to 2-3 times daily. Ordered lipid panel to assess need for medication adjustments. Continue metformin 500 mg daily. Discussed dietary modifications; patient attempting to watch carbohydrate intake but not tracking specifically. Diet described as "decent but could be better."
